message:
Bridge Retrofit Engineer, Structural Dynamicist, Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead and Manager, comfort for this 1.9 Hz mode must use Human-Induced Vibration of Steel Structures, defined as Human-Induced Vibration of Steel Structures (HIVOSS), and French footbridge vibration guide, defined as French footbridge vibration guide (Setra), bands because 1.9 Hz lies inside the critical vertical walking range.

In plain words resonance at walking pace forces a band verdict not a feel judgement. Retrofitted 0.67 m/s2 from the crowd build-up simulation (E45) sits inside Medium 0.5 to 1.0 m/s2 versus bare 8.28 m/s2 from the bare-acceleration calculation (E43) which is unacceptable above 2.5 m/s2, with 0.67 m/s2 at 0.068 times gravity a small fraction against 8.28 m/s2 at 0.844 times gravity near body weight outside everyday feel.

Bridge Retrofit Engineer, Structural Dynamicist and Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead, Maximum below 0.5 m/s2 would cost larger mass and tighter tuning upkeep for little operational gain over Medium on this crowded Class III case, so Medium is the buildable trade.

In plain words chasing Maximum needs more damper and more maintenance access while Medium already removes the fall-risk shake. I take from the A Review on Comfort of Pedestrian Bridges Under Human-Induced Vibrations (E48) that a Multiple Tuned Mass Damper, defined as Multiple Tuned Mass Damper (MTMD), system shows stronger robustness under random pedestrian loads, which from comfort means the twin 400 kg Tuned Mass Damper, defined as Tuned Mass Damper (TMD), holding 0.476 to 0.526 m/s2 from the detuning sweep (E70) with 6.20 percent effective damping from the free-decay simulation (E17) keeps the Medium verdict under drift, serviced from below by Below Bridge Access Vehicle, defined as Below Bridge Access Vehicle (BBAV), with the instrumented walk-through kept as after-build bench test.

Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead, I lock deck appearance as a countable topology ban separate from style: zero hardware items and zero added symbols above the walking surface, all named steel between the girders below the soffit within girder depth at midspan per the layout sketch (E55).

In plain words anything counted above the deck fails appearance even when comfort passes. Above the walking surface I count zero added items against a permitted count of zero on the agreed chain girders to High-Strength Friction-Grip, defined as High-Strength Friction-Grip (HSFG), clamp bolts to transverse cross-beam to springs plus dampers to twin masses to stops, jointly confirmed with Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead and Bridge Retrofit Engineer. I am ready, because Medium comfort, robustness, and the zero-above-deck ban all survive my strongest objection.
